problems.name: Each potter's copy is theirs alone
problems.summary: A friend's copy off the phone can be read and replaced only by that friend, with no account and nothing to remember.

problems.name: A replaced or wiped phone gets its records back
problems.summary: A potter with an empty phone can get their pots and photos back without having kept a code.

problems.name: A copy is made although iPhones only copy while open
problems.summary: Records reach a second place soon enough that a lost phone costs little, without any background copy.

problems.name: A lost or leaked secret does not end the copy's safety
problems.summary: A potter whose phone is lost or whose secret leaks is left with neither a stranger reading their pots nor no way back.

problems.name: A bad copy does not replace a good one
problems.summary: An update bug, a cleared store or a second install cannot overwrite a good copy off the phone with an empty or older one.

dimensions.problem: Each potter's copy is theirs alone
dimensions.name: What proves a copy is the potter's

options.name: A random secret the app makes
options.description: On first use the app makes a long random secret (at least 120 bits), keeps it on the phone and sends it with each copy; whoever holds it can read and replace that potter's copy.

options.name: A link the maintainer sends each friend
options.description: The maintainer makes one link per friend carrying a long random secret and sends it in a message; the friend taps it once and the app keeps the secret, with no typing.

options.name: A passkey on the potter's device
options.description: The app registers a passkey against a random handle, and the store releases a copy only to the holder of that passkey.

options.name: No server copy, only files
options.description: Nothing is sent to a server; every copy off the phone is a file the potter saves where they choose.

dimensions.why_it_matters: Without accounts something other than a sign-in has to say whose copy this is, and each choice puts a different job on the maintainer or the potter.

dimensions.problem: Each potter's copy is theirs alone
dimensions.name: How the secret reaches the installed iPhone app

options.name: A cookie the server sets
options.description: The server sets a cookie holding the secret when the link opens in Safari; on iOS 17.2 and later, Add to Home Screen copies cookies into the new web app once, and the app moves the secret into its own storage.

options.name: The secret is made in the installed app
options.description: The app makes or accepts the secret only when opened from the home screen; in a Safari tab it logs nothing and says to install first.

options.name: A file from the Safari tab
options.description: Pots logged in a tab are saved as a file there and opened in the installed app, which then has its own secret.

dimensions.why_it_matters: On iPhone a Safari tab and the installed app are separate stores, so a secret made in Safari is not in the app the friend then installs.

dimensions.problem: Each potter's copy is theirs alone
dimensions.name: How the stored copy is protected

options.name: Readable behind the secret
options.description: The store keeps records and photos as they are, protected only by the secret or passkey.

options.name: Encrypted at rest under a server key
options.description: The server encrypts each copy with a key it keeps outside the stored data, so a leaked disk or backup shows nothing readable.

dimensions.why_it_matters: The maintainer is comfortable being able to read friends' pots, so the choice is about what a leak of the store alone would show.

dimensions.problem: Each potter's copy is theirs alone
dimensions.name: Where the copy is kept

options.name: A file the potter saves
options.description: A button makes one file of records and photos and hands it to the share sheet or a download, so the potter chooses where it goes.

options.name: The maintainer's server
options.description: The app posts a copy to a small store the maintainer runs whenever it is open and online.

options.name: The potter's own cloud drive
options.description: The app writes a copy to a cloud drive the potter already has, after the potter allows it.

dimensions.why_it_matters: Where a copy sits decides who can reach it and what the maintainer must keep running, and more than one place can be used.

dimensions.problem: A replaced or wiped phone gets its records back
dimensions.name: How the records come back

options.name: The maintainer sends the link again
options.description: The friend messages the maintainer, who sends that friend's link or issues a new one tied to the same copy, and the friend taps it on the new phone.

options.name: Open a saved file
options.description: The potter opens a saved file from the share sheet or a picker and the app imports it.

options.name: Scan from the old phone
options.description: While the old phone still works it shows a code the new phone scans to receive the records.

dimensions.why_it_matters: A copy nobody can restore is not a recovery, and with nothing for the potter to remember the way back rests on the maintainer, a file or the old phone.

dimensions.problem: A copy is made although iPhones only copy while open
dimensions.name: When the copy is made

options.name: Each time the app opens online
options.description: On launch and when the phone reports it is online again, the app copies anything new.

options.name: After each save while online
options.description: Each save of a pot, stage change or photo is sent as soon as it is stored, when a connection exists.

options.name: A button the potter taps
options.description: A Save a copy now button makes a copy of everything, as a file or to the server, on demand.

options.name: A reminder when the last copy is old
options.description: The app shows when the last copy was made and a nudge once it is older than a limit the potter can see.

dimensions.why_it_matters: iPhones cannot copy in the background, so the moments a copy happens and how visible they are decide the gap; the maintainer is not sure yet whether a button with a reminder is acceptable.

dimensions.problem: A lost or leaked secret does not end the copy's safety
dimensions.name: What happens when the secret is lost or leaked

options.name: Nothing can be done
options.description: A lost secret means the copy cannot be opened; a new secret starts an empty copy.

options.name: The maintainer can reset a friend's copy
options.description: The maintainer hands a friend a new secret for the same copy after checking by message who they are.

options.name: A secret the potter can replace
options.description: From the app the potter makes a new secret, which moves the copy and invalidates the old one.

dimensions.why_it_matters: With nothing for the potter to hold, recovery rests on the maintainer or the platform, and each choice trades the maintainer's time against the risk of loss.

dimensions.problem: A bad copy does not replace a good one
dimensions.name: How earlier copies are kept

options.name: Only the latest copy
options.description: Each new copy replaces the one before.

options.name: The last few dated copies
options.description: The store keeps the last few copies with their dates and the app can restore an older one.

options.name: Merge pot by pot
options.description: Each pot has its own identity and last-changed time, and a copy adds or updates pots rather than replacing the lot.

dimensions.why_it_matters: A copy that mirrors the phone can copy a loss, and two installs on one iPhone are normal, so how copies are kept decides whether such events can be undone.
